behm-16x20-gable-garage.cons[7]: Not usable as drawn in high-wind/coastal, high-seismic (category D+) or heavy-snow (>30 psf) areas, and CA/FL/NY/WA may require a stamped set - meaning extra engineering cost on top of the $499. howtospecialist-16x20-gable.cons[0]: VERIFIED CUT-LIST ERROR - DO NOT CUT AS PRINTED: items A and B list 192 in. for the 5 skids and the 2 outer rim joists; both must be 240 in. (20 ft). The dimensioned drawings settle it - the floor-frame drawing reads 240 in. on the rim joist and 189 in. on the joists and its chain (2 x 13 3/4 + 13 x 14 1/2 clear + 16 x 1 1/2) closes on exactly 240 in.; the skid drawing is dimensioned 240 in.; the shopping list buys 20 ft stock for both; the floor sheathing (8 full + 4 half sheets = 320 sq ft), the 18 siding sheets (576 sq ft = 72 ft of wall x 8 ft) and the 11 trusses at 24 in. o.c. (= 240 in.) all confirm a 20 ft length. Cut to 192 in. and you build a 16x16 floor that the 240 in. side walls overhang by 4 ft, wasting 5 skids and 2 rim joists. The WALL dimensions are correct as published: 240 in. side-wall plates with a 233 in. cap, 185 in. gable-end plates with a 192 in. cap lapping the corners.
howtospecialist-16x20-gable.data_confidence: high - full text, lettered cut lists and shopping lists for all three parts were read from live Wayback captures (200) of the original pages, the dimensioned framing diagrams (floor frame, skids, all four walls, trusses) were downloaded and read visually, the $8 PDF price and no-refund policy came from the Gumroad product JSON, and the hero render was confirmed byte-identical to the plan's own image. The 192-vs-240 in. cut-list conflict is resolved: the diagrams, the shopping list, the sheathing/siding counts and the 11-truss layout all close on 240 in. (20 ft) for the skids and rim joists, so the printed 192 in. is a typo. Remaining soft spots are only fields the source genuinely never publishes (pitch as X/12, overall height, cost, skill level).
howtospecialist-16x20-gable.floor_framing: Floor frame is 240 in. x 192 in. Two 2x6 rim joists at 240 in. (20 ft) long - cut-list item B misprints these as 192 in. - carry 16 pieces of 2x6 at 189 in. spanning the 16 ft width at 16 in. o.c. (drawn chain: 2 x 13 3/4 in. + 13 x 14 1/2 in. clear + 16 x 1 1/2 in. of joist = exactly 240 in.). Decking is 3/4 in. plywood, 8 sheets at 48x96 in. plus 4 at 48x48 in. = 320 sq ft, screwed with 1 5/8 in. screws every 8 in. along the joists. Joist hangers and structural nails for the skid ties are in the hardware list.
howtospecialist-16x20-gable.foundation: On-grade skid foundation: 5 pieces of 4x4 at 240 in. (20 ft) long running the length of the building - cut-list item A misprints them as 192 in., while the shopping list correctly buys 5 pieces at 20 ft - set on a leveled, compacted gravel bed and spaced across the 16 ft width so the 189 in. joists bear on all five. The drawn clear spacings (45 3/4 + 43 3/4 + 43 1/2 + 43 3/4 in., plus 5 x 3 1/2 in. of skid = 194 1/4 in.) overrun the 192 in. floor width by 2 1/4 in., so the spacing has to be trimmed on site. Floor frame is toenailed or rafter-tied down to the skids. No slab, piers or frost footings, and no anchoring/tie-down detail is given.
howtospecialist-16x20-gable.summary: A free, fully-published 3-part plan for a 320 sq ft gable storage shed / workshop on 4x4 skids: 8 ft walls, 2x4 studs at 24 in. OC, T1-11 siding, two 36x36 in. windows in one 20 ft side wall, and double doors centered in the 16 ft gable end. The roof is eleven site-built 2x6 trusses at 24 in. OC with 1/2 in. plywood gussets, clear-spanning the 16 ft width so the interior has no posts. Each part page publishes a lettered cut list plus a lumber shopping list and tool list with no email gate, which makes it unusually good source data for a real build. Main caveats: cut-list items A and B misprint the two longest members - the 5 skids and the 2 outer rim joists must be 240 in. (20 ft), not the 192 in. printed, as the dimensioned floor and skid drawings, the shopping list, the sheathing and siding counts and the 11-truss layout all confirm; the trusses are not engineered or stamped; and pitch is published only as a 30-degree angle, with no overall height or load rating given.
howtospecialist-16x20-gable.wall_framing: 2x4 studs at 24 in. OC, single bottom plate plus double top plate; outside plate dimensions 192 x 240 in. The two long 20 ft side walls have 240 in. bottom and first top plates plus a 233 in. cap plate held back 3 1/2 in. at each end; the two 16 ft gable-end walls have 185 in. plates (192 in. minus the 3 1/2 in. thickness of each side wall) and fit between the side walls, with a 192 in. cap plate lapping 3 1/2 in. onto each side wall to lock the corners. Studs are 91 1/2 in. 2x6 double headers over openings with a 1/2 in. plywood spacer sandwiched between and locked with 2 1/2 in. screws; front door rough opening is 72 x 86 in. under a 75 in. 2x6 double header. The 240 / 233 / 185 / 192 in. plate set closes exactly and is correct as published - the cut-list error is confined to the skids and rim joists.

icreatables-16x20-dormer.roof: Gable roof at 10/12 pitch with a 5/12 shed dormer. Site-built rafters from 2x8s (19 @ 12'-0"), 2x8 loft/dormer rafters (7 @ 10'), 2x10 ridge board (22'), 2x4 collar ties (11), 2x4 sub-fascia, 7/16" OSB roof sheathing (18 sheets), 18 Simpson H2.5 hurricane ties. NOT engineered trusses — rafters are cut on site from angles given in the plans. 10" overhang on sides and gable ends. 25-year asphalt shingles over 15 lb felt (~5 squares). Roof snow load 40 psf. Caveat: the page prose says the roof "is sheeted with 1/2" O.S.B." while the materials list specifies 7/16" — a vendor internal contradiction; 7/16" is the itemized quantity.

icreatables-16x20-gable.summary: A 320 sq ft (16' x 20') gable storage-shed plan set from iCreatables, drawn as a conventionally framed mini-building: 2x4 walls at 16" o.c. with a double top plate and 8'-1" wall height (standard 92-5/8" studs), 2x6 floor joists with 3/4" T&G OSB over treated 6x6 skids, or a concrete slab as the alternate foundation. The 16' roof span is carried by 11 plant-manufactured, engineered common trusses at 4/12 pitch that you order from a local truss plant, with a 16" overhang all around and 25-year asphalt shingles. As drawn it has a 3068 prehung single door plus a 6068 prehung double door and one optional 5'-0" x 4'-0" window, with T1-11 siding. Delivery is an instant-download PDF (8-1/2 x 11 sheets you print at home) or mailed prints, and iCreatables publishes the complete materials list as a free public PDF before you buy.

icreatables-16x20-modern-studio.wall_framing: 2x4 studs at 16" on center with a double top plate, "just like a home is framed"; 7/16" OSB wall sheathing (24 sheets); 2x6 headers (8'-0" x3 and 20'-0" x2). Studs come in mixed lengths — 8'-0" (54), 9'-0" (14), 10'-0" (12) and 12'-0" (2) — plus 2x4 plates in 16'-0" (8, short walls) and 20'-0" (5, long walls) and ten 8'-0" door trimmers. The mixed stud lengths are driven by the two 16' END walls, which carry the sloping top plates: because the I-joist rafters span the 16' direction, the short (7'-7") and tall (10'-1 3/4") walls are the two 20'-long walls and both have level top plates.

icreatables-16x24-gambrel-barn.permit_notes: Drawn to IRC prescriptive-code practice and "regularly used to apply for building permits", but with NO engineer stamp — the site is explicit: "Do the plans have engineering? No, the plans do not come with an engineers stamp." High snow/wind/seismic areas need a locally licensed engineer to review and stamp. Site notes IBC 105.2 exempts detached accessory structures under 120 sq ft, so at 384 sq ft a permit is almost certainly required. The vendor also warns on its garage-plans page that "The Larger Sheds are in a grey area of information between a house and a shed", and that its separate garage plans carry extra content (braced wall panels, hold-downs, full footing/stem-wall plans, electrical) that some departments demand at this size. No snow-load or wind-load rating is stated on this plan page.

shedplans-16x20-gable.cons[900]: Same design sold twice under one company: Mediage LLC also lists this exact plan through its parent brand Craftcamp as '16x20 Workshop Shed Plans Gable Roof' at the same $19.99 (https://craft.camp/p/16x20-garden-shed-plan/), and the free 14-step edition is the same document on both sites (filename SKU SHED33 matches the Shedplans.org SKU SHED33). Prefer the craft.camp free copy - unencrypted, higher resolution, typo fixed - over the AES-256 copy-blocked Shedplans one. Shedplans' own product page no longer links the free edition at all (the free-vs-premium table is HTML-commented out) and its 'Free shed plans' nav link now sends you off-site to craft.camp, so you only find the free PDF if you already know the URL.
shedplans-16x20-gable.cons[901]: No designer is credited anywhere, so you cannot check the design against a named professional. The About page offers only 'our team of professionals has more than 5 years of experience' and 'our designers are all certified Autodesk pros'; the PDF's metadata Author is the website itself ('Shedplans.org', or 'Craft.camp' on the mirror), created 2018-08-06 in a UTC+03:00 timezone with no individual named. Joseph Truini - the genuinely credentialed shed author the site leans on - is billed as 'Main Editor' for site articles, not as the author of this plan set, so do not read his name as an endorsement of these drawings.
shedplans-16x20-gable.format: Instant PDF download (premium, $19.99). The identical 14-step free edition is published with no email gate by BOTH company brands: https://shedplans.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/16x20-Garden-Shed-Plan-Free.pdf (19 pages, A4, AES-256, print allowed / copy blocked, 1,714,611 bytes) and - the better copy - https://craft.camp/wp-content/uploads/2024/Free%20plans/16x20-Garden-Shed-Plan-Free-SHED33.pdf (20 pages, A4, unencrypted, 9,545,854 bytes, higher-resolution art, same step text with the 'coop' typo fixed).

shedplans-16x20-gable.pros[900]: The full free edition is mirrored - in a better copy - by the parent brand: craft.camp publishes the identical 14-step PDF unencrypted, at higher image resolution, with the 'coop' typo fixed, listed openly on https://craft.camp/free/shed-plans/ with no email gate. So you can read every dimension in this design before deciding whether the $19.99 materials/cut list is worth it.
shedplans-16x20-gable.roof: Gable, site-cut stick framing (no engineered trusses): 'cut thirty four rafters 9'-5 1/2" long' from 1 1/2" x 5 1/2" (2x6) PT lumber, 'fifteen collar ties 7'-2 1/4" long' from 2x4 PT, and a ridge board of 3/4" x 7 1/4" PT board 20' long; rafters drawn at 16 spaces of 1'-1 1/2" (~15-16 in. o.c.), joined with 2x3" (3-inch) wood screws. Plywood sheathing, building paper, metal drip edge and asphalt shingles; 'You will need 400 Sq Ft of asphalt shingle roofing.' Pitch is never stated. About 5:12 is the only value consistent with the published 11'-6" overall height (94.5" half-span x 5/12 = 39.4" rise on top of a ~96" top-plate height gives ~136" vs the stated 138"), and the 9'-7" x 20'-5" roof planes then imply roughly 12" of horizontal overhang (2 x 9.583 x 20.417 = 391 sq ft, matching the 400 sq ft shingle call-out). Treat the pitch as unconfirmed and lay the rafter out yourself.
shedplans-16x20-gable.unknowns[900]: whether the premium edition's revised figures supersede the free edition - craft.camp's premium copy advertises 230 clay bricks, 17 floor joists and a 12 ft height where the free 14-step PDF specifies roughly 285 bricks, fifteen joists and 11'-6"
shedplans-16x20-gable.wall_framing: 2x4 (1 1/2" x 3 1/2") plus some 3 1/2" x 3 1/2" posts, all specified as pressure-treated. Front wall: 20' top plate, two 7'-4" bottom plates, sixteen 6'-11" studs, a 5'-4" door header and three 11" cripples. Back wall: seventeen 6'-11" studs, two 20' plates, studs drawn at 1'-1 1/2" clear (~15 in. o.c.). Side walls: 15'-5" long, twelve 6'-11" studs, two 3'-4" boards for the window header and rough sill, four 2'-10 1/2" studs and four 5 1/2" cripples. Plates are screwed, not nailed: 'Connect the beams with 2x4" wood screws' - the PDF's notation is gauge x length (2.2 '8x5" wood screws' = #8 x 5"; 7.7 / 9.5 / 10.4 '6x1" wood screws' = #6 x 1" for hinges), so 2x4" means a 4-inch screw. Nails and staples do appear elsewhere: 2" galvanized nails for siding shields (7.6, 13.4), 1/2" galvanized nails for window beading (9.4), and 'an industrial stapler' for shingles (8.4).

sheds-unlimited-16x20-gambrel-barn.cons[0]: Brutal price cliff at the 16' width — and it is real vendor pricing, not a typo. 14×20 wood siding is $8,876 and 16×20 is $14,879: +68% money for +12.5% floor area. The same step appears in every Sheds Unlimited kit line on their own 14×20-vs-16×20 kit-comparison pages (MiniBarn $7,298→$12,539, Standard Workshop $8,018→$12,863, Saltbox $8,876→$13,796, Classic Workshop $9,457→$14,090, single-car garage $8,844→$14,574) and in their assembled-building grid too, yet no page explains it. The step tracks WIDTH, not size: 14×48 (672 sq ft) is $17,934 while 16×20 (320 sq ft) is $14,879. Every peak-height table stops at "15'6" wide", so the likely driver is that 16'-wide buildings leave their one-piece road-delivery envelope — but the vendor never says so. Practical upshot: if your site allows 14' wide, 14×24 at $10,170 gives you 336 sq ft for $4,709 LESS than the 320 sq ft 16×20.
sheds-unlimited-16x20-gambrel-barn.data_confidence: High on identity, pricing and framing spec. The canonical URL was confirmed from archived HTML; the kit-page 16×20 prices ($14,170 wood / $18,484 vinyl) are byte-identical across snapshots 2025-11-07 and 2026-03-11. The price was then independently validated as a genuine DIY-kit figure rather than an assembled/installed figure: all 118 cells of the kit grid equal the matching cells of the assembled Standard MaxiBarn grid (snapshot 2026-04-14) times exactly 1.0500, and the vendor's FAQ states the packaged kit costs the same as the assembled building. The 14′→16′ price cliff was confirmed to be systematic across all five of the vendor's other kit lines on their own 14×20 and 16×20 kit-comparison pages, so it is vendor pricing policy, not a data error. Currency: a uniform 5% list increase landed between Feb and May 2026 (proven kit-to-kit on the sibling garage kit), so the current 16×20 figures are $14,879 / $19,408. Medium only on the physical envelope: every peak-height table stops at 15′6″ wide, so the actual built width and peak height of the "16×20" remain undocumented, and the vendor publishes no explanation for the 16′ premium.
sheds-unlimited-16x20-gambrel-barn.price: $14,879 for 16×20 with painted engineered-wood (SmartSide / Smart Panel T1-11) siding; $19,408 for 16×20 with Double 4" Dutchlap vinyl — the vendor's post-April-2026 list prices. The kit page itself last showed the pre-increase figures ($14,170 wood / $18,484 vinyl, snapshot 2026-03-11) before Sheds Unlimited applied a uniform 5% increase across the whole catalogue. This is a DIY-kit price, not an assembled-only or delivered-and-installed price: the vendor states "the price of the packaged kit will be the same as a normal, assembled building", and every cell of the kit grid equals the matching cell of the assembled Standard MaxiBarn grid exactly ×1.0500. Shipping (mileage-based, never published), site prep / pad, and permits ($1,300 if Sheds Unlimited handles them) are all extra.

shedsunlimited-16x20-gable.cons[2]: The 16'-wide price grid has a huge unexplained step, and it is real vendor pricing rather than a listing error. 14×20 is $8,844 but 16×20 is $15,303 — 73% more money for 12.5% more floor area, and 16×20 nearly matches 14×48 ($16,755) at less than half the area. The identical step shows up in all five of Sheds Unlimited's other kit lines and in their assembled-building grids, but no page explains it; every peak-height table stops at "15'6" wide", so the likely driver is that 16'-wide buildings exceed their one-piece road-delivery envelope. If a 16-ft width is not a hard requirement, 14×24 ($9,811, 336 sq ft) is dramatically better value for the same usable area.
shedsunlimited-16x20-gable.price: $15,303 for 16×20 with engineered wood (SmartSide / Smart Panel T1-11) siding; $20,235 for 16×20 with Double 4" Dutchlap vinyl siding — current, and confirmed as a DIY-kit price on a second vendor page: /kit-sizes/16x20-shed-kits/ listed this same product at $14,574 wood / $19,271 vinyl before the vendor's uniform 5% list increase (×1.05 gives exactly $15,303 / $20,235).
